FN-ARRN6QS-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 216
Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund Sponsor: Senator Clyde Chambliss
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 03/17/2025
Senate Bill 216 as introduced would allow certain firemedics personnel retired under the
Employees’ Retirement System (ERS) to return to work, without suspension of their retirement
allowance, as a firemedic with any employer participating in ERS provided that the
compensation does not exceed $52,000 per year. In addition, the compensation cap established
by this bill for these retired firefighters and emergency medical services are repealed December
31, 2030, unless extended by an act of the Legislature.
This bill could increase the obligations of several state and local agencies or entities that employ
these retired firefighters or emergency medical services by an undetermined amount dependent
upon any additional compensation paid to these retirees under the provisions of this bill.

FN-ARRN6QS-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 216
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Clyde Chambliss
Analyst: Cary Dean Date: 04/22/2025
Senate Bill 216 as passed the Senate would allow certain retirees under the Employees’
Retirement System (ERS) to return to work, without suspension of their retirement allowance,
as a firemedic, provided that their compensation does not exceed $52,000 per year.
This bill could increase the obligations of state or local agencies that employ these individuals
by an undetermined amount dependent upon any additional compensation paid to these retirees
under the provisions of this bill. This bill could also increase the obligations of RSA by an
undetermined amount dependent on the actuarial value associated with any individuals that
retire and return to work as a firemedic and earn compensation above the current retiree
compensation cap of $39,000 but less than the new maximum of $52,000 proposed by this bill
but who would not otherwise have retired and received retirement benefits absent the provisions
of this bill.
This bill would also extend the sunset provision for the employment of certain ERS retirees
without suspension of their ERS retirement from December 31, 2026, under current law, to
December 31, 2030.
